title: Calls for police shootings to be investigated by independent organizations
article: Police shootings in Quebec should be investigated by a review board composed entirely of civilians, Quebec's Ligue des droits et libertés and an organization that protects the rights of the homeless said Monday.

The call for an end to one force police being assigned to probe shootings committed by another department comes four months after a homeless man and passerby were fatally shot by Montreal police in a failed attempt to subdue the former.

Ligue co-ordinator Nicole Filion said that while Public Security minister Robert Dutil was open to changing the present system of investigating police shootings, the suggestion that a review board include police and civilians was off the mark.
Filion argued that lawyers, either prosecutors or defense, could serve on the board and not be a part of "the blue brotherhood" of police.
"It could be (staffed by) lawyers...but civilians could also be trained. If police can be trained to conduct investigations, civilians can, as well."
Last June 7, 40-year-old Mario Hamel and Patrick Limoges, 36, died after Montreal police opened fire on Hamel in an apparent attempt to defend themselves.

Police alleged that Hamel, who had a history of psychiatric problems, had been ripping into garbage bags near Ste. Catherine and St. Denis Sts. and that he charged at them repeatedly with a knife when confronted. After attempting unsuccessfully to subdue him with pepper spray, the officers fired multiple rounds in his direction.
Limoges, a worker at nearby St. Luc Hospital, was on the other side of the street and was struck by a stray bullet or richochet.

The investigation of the shooting was conducted by the Surete du Quebec, which turned its findings over the province's bureau of criminal prosecutions two weeks ago where it is being is studied to determine if charges are warranted.
